newsitem.title: USA: Unusual bowtie tribute to Sen. Paul Simon.
newsitem.headline: Unusual bowtie tribute to Sen. Paul Simon.

text.p: In a dapper tribute to a retiring colleague, nearly every member of the Senate appeared on the floor Tuesday wearing a bow tie -- the sartorial trademark of Sen. Paul Simon.
"To say that the senior senator from Illinois has influenced us all in an understatement," said Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle, sporting a blue bow tie decorated with white stars.
Simon, arriving on the floor for a vote to find his colleagues wearing the bow ties, was greeted with applause. The Illinois Democrat is retiring after two six-year terms in the Senate.
Arkansas Democratic Sen. David Pryor and Florida Republican Sen. Connie Mack of Florida came up with the idea and Pryor ordered the matching clip-ons from a Little Rock firm.

Sen. Robert Byrd, a West Virginia Democrat, was the only male member of the Senate who declined to wear a bow tie. Three senators created an unusual effect by wearing bow ties over their ordinary ties.
Female senators wore matching scarves. Sen. Barbara Mikulski, a Maryland Democrat, wore a bow tie as well as the scarf.
